$comment: Single source of truth for the bridge command/event contract (BE-1, issue #271, epic #246, ADR 0004). C++ ties to these values via static_asserts in crates/mib-bridge/src/shim.cpp; Rust via crates/mib-bridge/tests/contract.rs; TypeScript via the generated desktop/src/bridgeContract.ts (scripts/gen_bridge_contract.py --check fails CI on drift). All changes must be additive: append values, never renumber or repurpose.

frame_packet.timestamp_semantics: legacy raw timestamp_ns; unit and clock validity unavailable
frame_packet.identity_semantics: Live raw frames carry CaptureService generation and FrameStore epoch stamped atomically with pixels. Zero means unavailable; raw processing config is inapplicable. Review/background have separate explicit source ownership and zero capture identities. Monitoring cell crops (pull kinds 5 and 6, ABI 41) are backend-owned copies with zero capture identities: frame_index and timestamp_ns are the row's; the run, frame and object that name the cell are the request's (monitoring_cells).

json_transport.event_loss_semantics: notification loss only; not acquisition loss

experiment_status_semantics.legacy_slots: validSaved = persistence committed; invalidSaved = 0 (split no longer tracked); droppedValid = persistence pending (admitted - committed - failed); droppedInvalid = persistence failed
experiment_status_semantics.typed_fields: startGeneration/persistence*/completion/terminal/finalizationOk are exact; completion is a run_completion_states value, Unknown until terminal
experiment_status_semantics.snapshot: fetch_experiment_status carries the full status (generations, fault code/message, completion reason); fetch_experiment_readiness carries the gate list with readiness_gate_statuses values and the generation a Start must present

request.source_paths: optional 1..256 source paths; independent readers; forbids explicit_destination

status.retained_partial_path: visible partial output with failure manifest, terminal only
status.results: per-file source_path/state/final_path/retained_partial_path/error for all attempted files; batch continues on failure and stops on cancellation

review_export_json.retention: latest export snapshot retained until next accepted submit
review_export_json.concurrency: one active export; busy submit rejected; cancel through operation_cancel; terminal after cleanup

checked_config_document.apply: path + required SHA256 baseline + image_processing-only JSON patch
checked_config_document.notes: No force overwrite; no startup-file selection changes; saved-only is not successful application.

preview_buffer_json.save_request: action save(default)|resize|background; save: output_root existing directory, format tiff|avi, first,last decimal-u64, range_mode index(default)|timestamp(raw source units), filter_empty:boolean, fps finite (0,1000]; resize: capacity decimal-u64 1..1000000, confirm_clear:boolean; background: index decimal-u64 Mono8; optional generation decimal-u64 precondition
preview_buffer_json.save_result: ok:boolean; output_path:string including retained partial path; error:string
preview_buffer_json.guards: idle experiment and stopped capture; exact retained range and supplied ring generation; resize available-memory budget, shrink clearing requires confirmation; active-kernel empty filter; unique destination directory; no overwrite; AVI has no per-frame timestamps

local_profiles.identity: SHA256 over exact config.json, optional egrabberConfig.js and profile.meta.json bytes; baseline required for duplicate, rename, archive and apply
local_profiles.persistence: Create stages a complete new directory; existing names never overwrite. Archive renames to hidden recoverable directory. Caller selects base directory. Changes serialize with experiment idle guard; not a cross-process CAS.
local_profiles.activation: Stopped capture/realtime and disabled autofocus; validate all supported settings before mutation; processing/buffer/realtime/delivery/calibration/autofocus configuration/validated ROI only; no hardware connection or script execution
local_profiles.response: ok, error?; profiles/warnings for list; profile for read/create/duplicate/rename; applied/message/profile_id/display_fps for apply; destination for archive; saved after create publication
local_profiles.startup: Successful apply persists .selection.json. Restore only exact aggregate revision; selection returns separate saved choice and actual runtime profile_selection provenance.
local_profiles.remote: profile_fetch_url HTTP(S), no credentials or redirects, 4 MiB, finite timeout; asynchronous outside bridge mutex. install_remote verifies SHA256, app version and processing contract, requires baseline/identity for replacement, preserves hidden full-directory backup, never applies settings.

request.source_path: existing HDF5, image folder or AVI path
request.count: nonnegative integer; 0 selects remaining subject to input budgets
request.synthetic_background: boolean; build shared quiet-tile background when no source background
request.roi: optional {x,y,w,h}; positive size, nonnegative origin, source bounded
request.image_processing: optional local config.json image_processing object; never applies to live settings
request.background_index: optional nonnegative source frame index, loaded independently
request.clear_background: discard saved source background before optional selection/synthetic build
request.max_input_mib: integer 1..16384; default 256; input pixels only, processing needs additional memory

review_reanalysis_json.status: review-export status vocabulary; own operation id; current settings, source ROI/background/identity, active core recorded

review_charts_json.description: all valid-file metrics; 128x128 density conserves every finite calibrated point; histogram exact; shared Qt math
review_charts_json.calibration: current backend pixel_to_micron; reference conditions labelled

review_reanalysis_preview: source_kind/source_path/dataset/index -> atomic Mono8 frame packet, independent reader, 64MiB frame limit

processing_core_management.trust: Existing portable cache/loader and shared Qt/Tauri compiled signer policy; selected index must match immutable manifest, ABI/contract/runtime/app bounds; never trust manifest-provided key alone.
processing_core_management.persistence: Atomic selection write in activateProcessingKernel preCommit callback; startup re-verifies signature/hash, failure marks selection unavailable; explicit bundled recovery honors pins.

render_review_overlay: source_path/valid/index/mode(0..4)/roi -> PNG bytes; independent same-reader image/mask/classification; shared Qt ProcessingOverlay; 64MiB source frame limit

monitoring_science.row_pixel_to_micron: exact factor passed to analyzeObjects for this row;0=unknown;host-only,not persisted HDF
monitoring_science.row_youngs_modulus: stored kernel LUT kPa result;zero unavailable
monitoring_science.calibrated_plot: valid finite rows with known positive analysis-time factor;never rescale old rows by current config
monitoring_science.reference_command: fetch_monitoring_chart_reference -> JSON curves [{modulus,points}],curve_source;shared bundled review/Qt resource;explicit reference conditions

pump_connect_model: pump, model (pump_models), port_name, baud_rate, modbus_address, microliters_per_rev -> CommandResult; either model can fill the Sample or Sheath slot; a peristaltic connect only reads registers 100-107; flow rates (µL/min or mL/min) convert to head speed with microliters_per_rev; out-of-range rates fail; purge runs at 100 rpm and stop restores the flow speed; syringe volume fails for peristaltic; fetch_pump_status adds model, microliters_per_rev, speed_rpm (v22)
stage_commands: Z stage (#464, ADR 0013 Amendment 1; ABI 30 = no homing). The stage is never homed. Enforced in the backend, not the shell: stage_move_to(target_um) / stage_move_by(delta_um) are refused until the operator set zero in the current controller power-up (stage_set_zero), outside the travel envelope around that zero (+/-1000 um by default; +/-(span/2 - 100 um) = +/-2900 um only after the operator declares mid-travel), and need whole micrometres; a target outside the envelope is refused, never clamped, and so is an approach overshoot that would leave it; stage_set_zero(mid_travel) is the only command that sets zero: one register write (position counter = 0), no motion, accepted only for an idle stage with no operation, e-stop or driver alarm, and without mid_travel only while the stage is inside the window set by the first zero of that power-up; it clears the previous declaration; an e-stop or driver alarm clears zero_set (an operator Stop does not); the controller's power-up token is compared on every idle poll and before every motion opcode, so a power cycle while connected drops the zero and its window (a window survives an e-stop, alarm or failed move, but not a new power-up); power_up_token_register 0 (config refuses it without allow_session_only_zero) turns that off and is reported as session_only_zero; limit bits only stop a move heading toward an active switch and gate nothing else; limits_verified (record written only by the bench tool zc300ctl verify-limits --supervised; no bridge, server or UI path can write it) clears a wiring-unverified badge and never widens the envelope; nothing else moves: stage_connect(port_name, usb_serial, modbus_address) is observe-only (identity, profile check, power-up token), stage_apply_profile only writes and saves controller configuration (and clears zero_set), discovery kind MotionStage only reads identity (FC04); stage_stop is always accepted, also during an experiment; every other stage command, stage_set_zero included, fails while an experiment is not idle. Moves return an operation id (operation_kind StageMove) whose cancel stops the axis; stage_set_zero returns none. fetch_stage_status -> {valid, enabled, connected, configured, zero_set, mid_travel_declared, session_only_zero, limits_verified, busy, model, serial, firmware, port_name, move_state (stage_move_states), position_um, limit_positive, limit_negative, home, emergency_stop, driver_alarm, span_um, envelope_min_um, envelope_max_um, last_error}; home is a raw controller input that floats on this stage and carries no information. On the remote server every stage command except stage_stop and fetch_stage_status is a CONTROL command.
soft_trigger_camera: Explicit MindVision camera software exposure trigger; shell requires armed Service mode, native command requires running MindVision camera and idle experiment; no automatic invocation

camera_alignment.set_camera_overview: overview bool -> CommandResult; MindVision and Aravis cameras; full sensor at the overview preset vs the saved experiment window; stops capture and realtime processing, swaps the frame store (8 frames in overview), restarts a capture that was running; rejected during experiment/recording; experiment readiness fails camera.mode while in overview
camera_alignment.save_camera_roi: x,y,width,height (sensor coordinates) -> CommandResult; bounds and steps from the camera; MindVision writes its profile, Aravis <data>/config/aravis-camera.json; applies at the next experiment-mode start
camera_alignment.fetch_platform_info: -> JSON {science: host|pl, host_processing, aravis, capabilities{instrument: desktop|pz7035, autofocus, trigger, host_background, frame_buffer, reanalysis, core_updates, egrabber_script, pl_identity, led_strobe, align_mode, run_mode, pump: null|{model, port, sample_address, sheath_address, microliters_per_rev}}}; science=pl when built with MIB_PL_SCIENCE (PZ7035 PS) or MIB_PL_SCIENCE=1 in the environment: apply_processing with realtime on fails, experiment start does not start the host pipeline, the host pipeline's readiness gates are replaced by science.pl
camera_alignment.set_instrument_mode: mode (align|run|idle), x, y -> CommandResult; PZ7035 only (#501 P1, v27). Order: LED off and U-Net cell path off; producer staged (align: full field 400 fps / 2299.7 us with PzHmax 232 = HMAX 232 / VMAX 800 / SHS 64, then the producer stopped and whole frames from the bridge preview slots as the live camera (needs expected-core.json feature align_whole_frame_preview and a matching BUILD_ID, results8 on; otherwise the banded fallback 500 fps / 1899.7 us = 116 / 1280 / 64 with the producer streaming); run: 512x96 at x snapped to 8, y to 4, 5000 fps / 150 us = 58 / 256 / 64); capture start (AcquisitionStart applies ROI, timing, S[9], receiver reset); align: LED 100/135 us (bands: 0/125 us); run: capture stopped, cell path on, latency cleared, LED 7/60 us. Refused during an experiment or recording, when the PL is not configured (DEVCFG PCFG_DONE) or not the U-Net cell image. In run, start_capture and set_camera_overview are refused and readiness has instrument.mode instead of the live-camera gates; mode idle (the unattended safe state the server applies when the last client has been gone for its grace time, v32 additive): LED off, cell path off, camera released, refused during an experiment or recording, and mode.idle reads true until the next switch
camera_alignment.sync_wall_clock: unixMs (ms since the epoch, the client's Date.now()) -> CommandResult; controller only. G14: a board without an RTC stamps saved files (start_time_ns, end_time_ns, the SSD run table) from the last client time plus the monotonic clock, so a later system-clock change cannot move a run. Times outside 2026..2100 are refused; a change under 2 s is jitter; during an experiment or recording the clock is kept. Files carry timestamp_wall_source (client_sync | board_clock_unsynced | system_clock) and timestamp_wall_offset_ns; fetch_instrument_status gains wall_clock{synced, source, offset_ns, last_sync_unix_ms}; both are bridge ABI 33
camera_alignment.fetch_ring_status: -> JSON {available (a ring is wanted and fits), reason (why not, or why the ring is invalid), frozen (STATE IDLE after STOP, FINAL = HEAD + 1, no sticky bit), invalid (RING_STALLED, RESET_GENERATION refused or FAULT: re-arm), stop_incomplete (STOP_STUCK: not frozen, the records below FINAL stay readable under the reader rule), restore_needed (STOP never reached IDLE within 1 s: the PL needs a restore), fault_cleared (the FAULT register value the automatic FAULT_CLEAR removed at the last Run start, 0 if none), fault_cleared_state (the bridge STATE, 6 = FAULT, that start cleared, also when the register read 0), run_frozen (the Run is stopped and its ring held for playback: by the operator's Stop, or, since ABI 37, by the end of an SSD run; Resume Run or the next experiment start discards the frames), capacity_frames, first_seq, last_seq (the readable range, inclusive), count, sensor_fps, state, head, epoch (ABI 37: the CONFIG_COMMIT epoch the ring's frame records carry, committed before every ARM so a frozen ring holds one value; while the ring is held after a Run stopped it is the value from the moment of the stop, since a Start commits a new epoch before it leaves the stopped Run; null when the status describes no valid ring), hold_note (ABI 37: why a held Run needs attention, e.g. the LED could not be switched off; empty otherwise)}; the same object is the `ring` block of fetch_instrument_status (ABI 34, #649 v1)
camera_alignment.fetch_ring_frame: seq (u64, a ring sequence) -> binary MIBR packet (error RING_FRAME_UNAVAILABLE: <outcome>: <why> when out of range, overwritten while copied, malformed or no ring): 48-byte LE header 'MIBR' | u16 version 1 | u16 header 48 | u64 seq | u64 frame id | u64 timestamp ticks | u32 tick Hz | u32 frame flags | u16 width | u16 height | u16 cells | u16 flags: bit0 mask present, bit1 results truncated, bit2 frame invalid, bit3 frame cut (MONO8 incomplete), bit4 mask incomplete; then gray (width*height), mask (width*height/8, 1 bit/px LSB first, row-major), cells x 19 u32 words (the 'MIBC' layout plus the payload validity: 0-14 unet_cells_v2 payload, 15 = y<<16|x, 16 = h<<16|w, 17 = cells<<24|index<<16|valid, 18 = payload validity mask: a word the mask leaves out is not available, not 0); read under the reader rule of pz7035 docs/FRAME_RING.md (the HEAD re-read after the copy) (ABI 34)
camera_alignment.ring_freeze: -> CommandResult; controller only; Stop in Run: the live session stops, the provider waits for the device's frozen state, the LED goes off and the ring is held for playback; refused outside Run, with an experiment or recording active, or when no ring is configured (ABI 34)
camera_alignment.fetch_run_fps: -> JSON {available, reason? (when not available), min_fps (1000), max_fps (5000), default_fps (5000), qualified_fps (5000: the only rate qualified on the board), fps (the configured Run rate, a whole number), exposure_mode (auto | manual), exposure_us (auto: the exposure that starts ~50 µs after XVS (SHS 64 at HMAX 58, 32 at HMAX 116), 150 at 5000 fps and lines x HMAX / 74.25 below, 949.87 at 1000 fps; manual: the requested exposure rounded to whole lines), hmax (58 above 2655 fps, else 116: the producer's own rule, told through PzHmax), vmax (floor(74.25 MHz / (hmax x fps))), shs, exposure_lines (vmax - shs), actual_fps (74.25 MHz / (hmax x vmax)), exposure_start_us / exposure_end_us / strobe_start_us / strobe_end_us (µs after XVS), strobe_overlaps, strobe_straddles_exposure_start, strobe_warning, allowed_exposure_min_us / allowed_exposure_max_us (the manual exposures the strobe window allows at this rate), qualified (fps == qualified_fps with the auto exposure), in_run, applied_fps / applied_exposure_us (the setting of the last Run entry, null outside Run), pending (the camera runs at another setting than the configured one: enter Run again), held (a stopped Run's ring is held)} (ABI 38)
camera_alignment.check_pz_camera_document: {text} -> JSON {ok, error? (names the key), and on ok the fields of fetch_run_fps describing the timing the document gives}; no side effects. The PZ7035 camera document is {"schema": "pz7035-camera/1", "run": {"frame_rate_hz": 1000..5000 (whole), "exposure_us": "auto" | number}}; unknown keys are errors and the LED strobe is not part of it (Service-only); a numeric exposure must start the exposure inside the strobe pulse (ABI 38)
camera_alignment.apply_pz_camera_document: {path, acknowledgeDiscardRing?} -> CommandResult; controller only; reads the PZ7035 camera document file (a regular file under 64 KiB, on the instrument), validates it as check_pz_camera_document does, stores the Run rate and exposure in the Aravis profile and, when the instrument is in Run, re-enters Run at the same window so they apply at once; otherwise they apply at the next Run entry. Refused during an experiment or recording, and in a stopped Run whose ring is held unless acknowledgeDiscardRing (the re-entry discards the buffered frames) (ABI 38)
camera_alignment.ring_resume: -> CommandResult; controller only; Resume Run: LED on, a new ring from sequence 0 (the buffered frames are gone) (ABI 34); also ends the stopped Run an SSD run leaves behind (ABI 37)
camera_alignment.fetch_ssd_status: -> JSON {configured (false: no pzrec/image configured, state ABSENT), state (ABSENT, INITIALISING, RECOVERING, READY, RECORDING, STOPPING, WEDGED, RUN_TABLE_FULL, RAW_FULL, UNFORMATTED), usable (READY: a run could start), active (RECORDING or STOPPING), reason (the UI text when not usable, empty when READY or RECORDING; a failing, hanging or garbled pzrec is WEDGED with its stderr here, never READY), last_error, raw_bytes, free_bytes, min_run_bytes, runs, next_run_id, table_entries, recovered_runs, recovered_ids, skipped_bad_entries (run-table entries the tail reclaim stepped over), open_run: null | {id, start_unix_ms, client_tag, wall_source, seen, empty_filtered, invalid_not_sampled, passed, written, dropped, failed, bytes_written, drain_kbps, first_frame_id, last_frame_id}}; read only (#667 S1, ABI 35): Studio runs the pzrec CLI (env MIB_PZREC and MIB_SSD_IMAGE) in a background thread, the call returns the last answer at once (INITIALISING before the first); a short {configured, state, usable, active, reason, last_error} is the `ssd` block of fetch_instrument_status
camera_alignment.ssd_export_begin: run, from, count -> JSON {ok, lease, run_id, records, bytes, max_seconds, argv[], run{start_unix_ms, tick_hz, first_ticks, last_ticks, first_frame_id, last_frame_id, seen, filter, written, client_tag, wall_source, reason, size_bytes, exact_drops}} | {ok: false, code (BUSY, UNAVAILABLE, NO_SUCH_RUN, RUN_DELETED, NOT_OFFERED, BAD_RANGE), reason}; NOT a WebSocket command: the HTTP route GET /ssd/runs/{id}/records is the only caller (#667, ABI 36). Takes the one export lease atomically against prepareRun (a Start in progress), the open run, STOPPING and a failed stop, and refuses with the reason unless the window shows IDLE (pzrec snapshot --window-only), the SSD is READY and the run is closed, not deleted, with a reliable record count (reason 7 recovered runs are not offered); from/count (0: the whole run) must lie inside the run's written records (refused, never clipped); bytes = records x 59,392; argv is the pzrec read command line (RUN before IMG, same IMG and options as start/stop, --summary), one argument per element; max_seconds bounds the download (2 x 25 s bounce-path commands + 35 s + bytes at 5 MB/s) and the lease expires by itself 60 s after it (the caller terminates its reader at the bound; run is the run table entry of the whole run, also for a from/count window, sent by the route as X-Run-* headers so a download is self-describing; exact_drops: filter ALL and seen equal to the frame id span, so drops_before must equal min(gap, 255)). While a lease is held prepareRun refuses (export in progress), the periodic pzrec refresh stands down and the storage.ssd gate fails
camera_alignment.ssd_export_end: lease, bytes_sent, outcome -> nothing; NOT a WebSocket command (#667, ABI 36): releases the lease after the reader process has exited; idempotent, an unknown or expired lease is a no-op; bytes_sent and outcome are for the log
camera_alignment.fetch_ssd_runs: -> JSON {ok, reason (why the table is not readable, empty when ok), runs: [{id, open, deleted, incomplete, start_unix_ms, wall_source (0 board clock unsynced, 1 client synced), client_tag, filter (0 all, 1 any result, 2 valid only), sampler_n, reason (0 clean, 1 drain fault, 2 stall, 3 length, 5 drain not provably stopped, 6 length limit, 7 recovered at mount, 8 aborted, 9 raw area full), counts_unknown (reason 7: the totals are not known, show no numbers), totals_inconsistent (the totals do not add up: seen = empty_filtered + invalid_not_sampled + passed and passed = written + dropped + failed; no numbers either), size_bytes ((end_lba - start_lba) x 512: the run's raw size on the SSD), recoveries, first_frame_id, last_frame_id, tick_hz, first_ticks, last_ticks, seen, empty_filtered, invalid_not_sampled, passed, written, dropped, failed}] oldest first; read only (ABI 35); the run being recorded is in fetch_ssd_status.open_run, not here
camera_alignment.set_service_mode: on bool -> CommandResult; the shell's Service / Commissioning mode latched in the backend (v27)
camera_alignment.set_instrument_led: delayUs, widthUs -> CommandResult; raw LED, refused unless set_service_mode(true), during an experiment, without a camera mode or outside its limits (run: delay 0-100, width 20-80 us; align: 0-400, 60-150 us; also in fetch_platform_info capabilities.led_limits); the next mode switch restores the preset (v27)
camera_alignment.fetch_run_preview: -> binary MIBC packet (run mode only, else error RUN_PREVIEW_UNAVAILABLE): 32-byte LE header 'MIBC' | u16 version 1 | u16 header 32 | u32 frame id | u16 width 512 | u16 height 96 | u16 listed | u16 flags | u16 cells | u16 blemishes | u32 dropped | u32 0; then gray (width*height), U-Net mask (width*height/8, 1 bit/px LSB first, row-major), listed x 18 u32 cell words (0-14 unet_cells_v2 payload, 15 = y<<16|x, 16 = h<<16|w, 17 = count<<24|rank<<16|valid); one PL cell capture (S[36]) of a single frame (v27)
camera_alignment.fetch_run_accounting: source (review | last_run) -> JSON; the reconciled run accounting (v31, #549). review = the file loaded for review (available false with a reason when none is open; recorded false for a raw recording or a legacy file without accounting; adds file_path), last_run = the run that finished last in this session (adds start_generation and receiver_auto_resets, the PL receiver self-heal auto-resets during the run, each of which loses frames, null on an image without the RXH1 block, and nofs_frames, the frames the PL dropped for want of a FrameStart during the run (results12), lost data, null without the counters; available false before any run). Fields: completion (experiment_completion value) and completion_name, completion_reason, reconciled, admitted (frames the run claimed: the true denominator), empty, processed, scientifically_rejected, processing_failed, store_overwritten, store_not_committed, store_malformed (a declared loss: booked ingress-error frames), cancelled_by_policy, pending_at_stop, sequence_gaps, objects_detected, persistence_admitted/committed/failed/pending_at_stop, fatal_error, fatal_message, malformed_warn_fraction (0.001). Read-only; not a control command
camera_alignment.fetch_instrument_status: -> JSON {available, error?, core{build_id, profile_id, abi_version, science_profile, profile_version, expected: null|{build_id, profile_id, commit, image, abi_major, abi_minor}, pinned_profile_id, build_match, profile_match: match|mismatch|unknown}, led{on, preset: run|align|custom|off, delay_us, width_us, guard_fault, guard_trips}, link{rates_valid (false for about 1.5 s after a mode switch), ingress_errors_per_s, ingress_errors_avg_per_s and ingress_errors_warn (the 5 s average above ingress_errors_warn_per_s; valid after a full window since the last mode switch), resyncs_per_s, bad_frames_per_s, dropped_per_s, ingress_errors_warn_per_s, resyncs_warn_per_s, bad_frames_warn and dropped_warn (true when bad frames exceed 1% / dropped frames 0.1% of the XVS frame rate for 5 s), bad_frames_warn_per_s, dropped_warn_per_s, rx_heal{present, gave_up, tries, auto_resets (receiver resets), fs_present, fs_seen, nofs_frames, nofs_lines (results12: RXH1 words 32-34, tear-safe; frames start only after a FrameStart line, nofs_frames = frames dropped for want of one), v2 (heal v2, results11+: CTRL2 word 24 non-zero), flag_clears, episodes, failed_episodes (v2 only, 0 otherwise)} (the PL receiver self-heal block, results9 RXH1 at P[256]; present false on results8; the counter is read until two consecutive reads match because it can tear), bridge_active (ARMED/RUNNING: dropped frames are judged only then, P[6] counts every frame while nothing consumes the bridge)}, sensor{xvs_period_clocks, fps, width, height}, latency{last_us, max_us, over_budget, frames}}; read-only (#501); available=false off the PZ7035 or when the PL bridge is not loaded; build_match is unknown without /etc/yofo/expected-core.json; profile_match compares PROFILE_ID with the pinned unet-c4-multiline-v1 weights; v27: mode{name: align|run|unknown, run_x, run_y, run_set (true once a Run switch succeeded in this process: run_x/run_y are then the operator's window, not the (0, 0) default), service, idle (true after the unattended safe state until the next mode switch), align_lock{receiver_clears, failures, last_stuck_p13 (P[13] read before the latest recovery attempt), pl_gave_ups (times the results9+ PL self-heal gave up and the host recovery took over), last_pl_gave_up_ms (from the stream start to the latest gave-up)} (Align ingress recoveries in this process, #629), align_source: bridge|bands|""} and storage{path, writable, ram, free_bytes, filesystem, warning} (recording target of the data dir; ram = tmpfs/ramfs, warning = "Recording to RAM: lost on power-off. Copy data off before shutdown. <N> GB free." or ""); results{available, running, frames, results, empty_frames, invalid_frames, truncated_frames, incomplete_frames, decode_errors, sequence_gaps, overruns, last_error}: the PL result stream provider's cumulative counters while an experiment runs (they restart with each run; the UI turns successive polls into frames/s, results/s and EMPTY/INVALID/truncated fractions), additive within the existing command
camera_alignment.fetch_camera_geometry: -> JSON {supported, overview, camera, sensor_width, sensor_height, roi{x,y,width,height}, width/height/offset_x/offset_y_increment, min_width, min_height, session{...}}; session is the last Aravis read-back (rate, limit, bands, delivered rate)

experiment_start_request.$comment: ABI 39 (#712, ADR 0015 items 1, 4, 5, 7): experiment_start(output_path, acknowledge_discard_ring, start_request_json); the transports take an optional string startRequestJson (the client's JSON text) and pass it on byte for byte: Tauri, mib-app-commands, the WebSocket server and cxx never decode it, only the backend parser does, so duplicate keys reach it and the bounds apply to the client's own bytes. Absent or null = no request. Bounds pinned in C++ by static_asserts in crates/mib-bridge/src/shim.cpp (backend/recording/RunStartIdentity.h) and in Rust by crates/mib-bridge/tests/contract.rs.
experiment_start_request.document: startRequestJson = JSON text of {experiment_id: UUID (8-4-4-4-12 hex, stored lowercase), run_index: 0..4294967295 (needs experiment_id), sample_ref: id into the experiment's sample sheet (needs experiment_id), operator: {id, name} (the operator the client selected, #393 phase 1, recorded with assurance "selected", not authentication; at least one of the two), calibration_record_id: the applied calibration record (ADR 0015 item 7), annotation: {sample, condition, experimental_unit, concentration: {value (finite, >= 0), unit} (both or null), channel, medium, temperature_c (declared, degrees Celsius), notes, free: {string: string}}}; every member optional, null = not declared. Strict: unknown or duplicate keys, wrong types, empty strings (use null), control characters (notes may hold tab, CR, LF), invalid UTF-8 and anything over a bound (max_request_bytes counts the client's bytes, whitespace included) are refused with the key named (outcome InvalidRequest, message "invalid start request: <key>: <why>"), never truncated; a refused request opens nothing. Recorded: the identity and operator as members of the run snapshot v3 (run_snapshot_json: experiment_id, run_index, sample_ref, operator{id, name, assurance}, calibration_record_id; null when not declared); the annotation once, at Start, in /experiment_annotation (@annotation_json, @annotation_schema_version), which is absent when the request had none; a failed annotation write fails the start (ProvenanceFailed) and removes the file.

experiment_command_reply.$comment: ABI 40 (#741): the typed outcome of an experiment command in its CommandResult reply, additive over ABI 39. C++ BackendCommandResult.experimentStartOutcome / experimentStopOutcome -> cxx BridgeCommandResult has_start_outcome + start_outcome / has_stop_outcome + stop_outcome (values pinned by static_asserts in crates/mib-bridge/src/shim.cpp) -> mib-app-commands CmdResult (Tauri and the WebSocket server alike) -> desktop/src/eventAdapter.ts decodeCommandResult. message is unchanged, so a caller that reads only ok and message keeps working.
experiment_command_reply.start_outcome: JSON number, an experiment_start_outcomes value; on every experiment_start reply the backend evaluated (Started, NotReady, StaleReadiness, AlreadyActive, StorageFailed, ProvenanceFailed, Busy, InvalidRequest); omitted from other replies and from a start that never reached the coordinator (backend not initialized, an exception), where only ok and message describe it. A refused start request is InvalidRequest (7): switch on it instead of the message prefix "invalid start request: ".
experiment_command_reply.stop_outcome: JSON number, an experiment_stop_outcomes value; on every experiment_stop and experiment_cancel reply the backend evaluated (Accepted, NotActive, Busy, RunMismatch); omitted otherwise. message stays "accepted" | "notActive" | "busy" for those; for RunMismatch it is the plain reason (experiment_stop_request).

experiment_stop_request.$comment: ABI 40 (#741): experiment_stop gains an optional expected start generation, so a client stops only its own run. Transports: dispatch.rs / WebSocket arg expectedStartGeneration, Tauri arg expected_start_generation, bridge.experimentStop(expectedStartGeneration?) in desktop/src/bridge.ts; cxx experiment_stop(has_expected_start_generation, expected_start_generation: u64); C++ ExperimentCommand.expectedStartGeneration -> ExperimentCoordinator::requestStop(cancelled, expected, refusal). experiment_cancel is unchanged.
experiment_stop_request.expected_start_generation: optional string, a canonical decimal u64 (json_transport encoding: no sign, no leading zero), the start_generation of the run to stop as fetch_experiment_status reports it; anything else is refused by mib-app-commands ("Invalid expectedStartGeneration", an error reply, nothing sent), absent or null = not given. Not given: stops whatever run is active, exactly as in ABI 39.
experiment_stop_request.semantics: With it, the coordinator compares it with the run it holds in the same critical section (its mutex, also held by start and by the worker's finalization) that accepts the stop; it never checks first and acts later. The run is held from the Active entry until its finalization ends (Active, Stopping, or Failed while a fatal finalization runs); a Starting run has no generation a client could have read and is never held. No run held (Idle, Failed, Starting) or a held run with another start_generation: stop outcome RunMismatch (3), ok false, message "stop refused: expected run <E>, but <run <N> is active | run <N> is stopping | run <N> failed and is finalizing | a new run is starting | no run is active>; nothing was stopped", and nothing changes. Matching: the outcome without the argument (Accepted; Busy while that run is stopping or its stop is queued; NotActive while it is failing). An accepted stop is consumed by the finalization of the run it named, and no run can start before that finalization ends (start also clears any stale stop request), so it can never stop a newer run.

monitoring_cells.$comment: ABI 41 (#716 A6a): per-row cell images for the live Monitoring view, backend-owned (C++ backend::services::MonitoringCellStore, owned by AppBackend; facade BackendFacade::fetchMonitoringCellsJson / pinMonitoringCellJson / unpinMonitoringCell / clearMonitoringCellPins / fetchMonitoringCellImage -> cxx fetch_monitoring_cells, monitoring_cell_pin, monitoring_cell_unpin, monitoring_cell_clear_pins, fetch_monitoring_cell_image (BridgeMonitoringCellImage) -> mib-app-commands (Tauri and the WebSocket server alike) -> desktop/src/bridge.ts). Caps pinned by static_asserts in crates/mib-bridge/src/shim.cpp; outcomes by monitoring_cell_pin_outcomes. Additive over ABI 40.
monitoring_cells.identity: A monitoring row is named by (start_generation, capture_epoch, frame_index, object_id). start_generation is the run that was active when the processing path appended the row to the monitoring ring (ExperimentCoordinator sets it before the run's accumulation starts and resets it to 0 when the run stops accumulating or its start is rolled back), 0 = outside a run. capture_epoch is the capture the row's frame came from (ProcessingService::monitoringCaptureEpoch; see capture_rules for when it moves on); it starts at 1, only grows and is never reused (values may be skipped). frame_index and object_id are the row's. Stable across snapshots: fetch_monitoring_snapshot rows carry start_generation and capture_epoch (canonical decimal strings; omitted from review metric rows). No two rows held at once share an identity.
monitoring_cells.commands: fetch_monitoring_cells (read; args none) -> JSON listing. monitoring_cell_pin (args expectedStartGeneration, captureEpoch, frameIndex: canonical decimal strings; objectId: integer) -> JSON pin reply. monitoring_cell_unpin (args startGeneration, captureEpoch, frameIndex, objectId) -> CmdResult (ok false + plain message when not pinned, saying so when the identity names an earlier capture whose pins were dropped). monitoring_cell_clear_pins (no args) -> CmdResult (message "cleared N pin(s)"). fetch_monitoring_cell_packet (args startGeneration, captureEpoch, frameIndex, objectId, layer: "image" | "mask") -> frame packet, pull kind monitoring_cell_image (5) or monitoring_cell_mask (6): the owned Mono8 crop or the same crop of the processed mask of a cell of the current capture, pins first, then the strip; an empty packet (flags 0) when the cell or that layer is not held (the listing says why); an error reply "CAPTURE_MISMATCH: <plain reason>" (error_codes.capture_mismatch) when captureEpoch is not the current capture, whatever the backend still holds. A malformed identity or layer is an error reply and nothing is sent to the backend. Pin, unpin and clear are control commands on the WebSocket server (a viewer gets VIEWER_ONLY): pins are one shared, bounded set per instrument.
monitoring_cells.listing: {valid, scope_start_generation (the latest run started, 0 before the first; pins belong to it), ring_start_generation (the strip's run context at this refresh: the active run, or 0 outside a run), ring_capture_epoch (the current capture; every listed strip cell and pin is of it), revision (bumps whenever the strip or the pins change), strip: [cell] oldest -> newest, pins: [cell] in pin order, last_capture_change: {capture_epoch (the capture that began), reason (plain words, e.g. "the camera stopped"), pins_dropped, strip_dropped} | null (no capture change since the backend started), stats: {strip_cells, strip_bytes, pins, pin_bytes, indexed_rows, peak_bytes, strip_admitted, strip_evicted, refreshes, last_refresh_us, last_source_us}, caps: {strip_max_cells, strip_max_bytes, max_pins, pin_max_bytes, crop_max_side, row_index_max}}; {valid: false} before init. u64 identities and counters are canonical decimal strings; counts bounded by a cap are numbers.
monitoring_cells.cell: {start_generation, capture_epoch, frame_index, object_id, timestamp_ns, valid, target_group, object_count, track_id, centroid_x, centroid_y, bbox: {x, y, w, h}, area (px^2), deformability, area_ratio, ring_ratio, youngs_modulus, pixel_to_micron, image: {width, height, crop_x, crop_y, source_width, source_height, has_mask, bytes} | null, no_image_reason: string | null}; exactly one of image and no_image_reason is non-null; non-finite numbers are null. Measurements are the row's as the processing path recorded them, never recomputed; geometry is in the coordinates of the row's image (see geometry).
monitoring_cells.pin_reply: {ok (Pinned, PinnedWithoutImage or AlreadyPinned), outcome (a monitoring_cell_pin_outcomes value; absent when the backend never evaluated the pin, e.g. before init), message, cell (the pin, or null when refused), revision}. Pinned: an owned crop (and mask when the row has one) that survives the monitoring ring. PinnedWithoutImage: the row's measurements only, message = the reason (the frame left the ring before the pin and only the bounded index of rows the snapshot served still describes it, or the instrument reports cells without images). AlreadyPinned: no change. RunMismatch: expected_start_generation is neither 0 nor the latest run started, or the row was detected in another run (or outside a run), or a run started while the pin was taken; nothing changes. NotFound: the backend holds neither the row nor its measurements. LimitReached: max_pins pins or pin_max_bytes bytes are held; a pin is never evicted to make room. CaptureMismatch: capture_epoch is not the current capture, or the capture changed while the pin was taken (see capture_rules); checked before every other rule; nothing changes.
monitoring_cells.strip: The most recently detected valid cells of the ring's current context (the active run's rows while one runs, rows outside a run otherwise, and only the current capture's), refreshed from the monitoring ring by fetch_monitoring_cells: at most strip_max_cells new crops per call, taken outside every lock; oldest evicted first when the count or strip_max_bytes is exceeded; a row of another run is dropped at the next refresh, a row of an earlier capture at the moment the capture changes (capture_rules); every eviction counts in stats.strip_evicted. monitoring_clear also clears the strip (and the row index); pins stay.
monitoring_cells.crop: The object's bounding box grown by max(crop_min_margin, the box's longer side / 2) on each side, at most crop_max_side square, shifted (never shrunk) to stay inside the row's source image (the processing ROI); an unknown box is centred on the centroid (else the image centre) with half the maximum side. Mono8: channel 0 of a multi-channel image, 16-bit scaled by 1/256; other formats have no image (reason given). The mask crop is the same rectangle of the processed mask when it has the image's size.
monitoring_cells.run_rules: Pins and the strip are dropped when a run starts (ExperimentCoordinator, at Active). A pin names its run: expected_start_generation must be 0 (rows outside a run) or the latest run started (scope_start_generation); any other is RunMismatch, so a stale client cannot pin into a newer run. The row's own start_generation must match it (a row of another run, or of none, is RunMismatch).
monitoring_cells.threading: Nothing runs on the acquisition/processing path: the ring's appends store one more 24-byte tag (run, capture epoch, geometry origin) in a preallocated array, with two compares (the frame's store generation and capture session, the capture backstop) under the lock they already hold. Readers take the ring's lock only to copy scalars and cv::Mat headers (refcount shares of frozen images), crop and clone outside every lock, then drop the shares under the ring's lock again (the lock its evictions take, so every free of a frame follows its readers in a lock order ThreadSanitizer can see; OpenCV's reference count is invisible to it). Store copies never leave the store: an image pull copies the crop under the store's mutex. The store's own mutex is never held while the ring is read; the current capture epoch is an atomic read before it is taken. A capture change is applied on the thread that made it (a camera mode switch, a camera session opening or closing, an ROI change, a realtime start), outside the ring's lock: the store drops the old capture's copies and frees them after its mutex is released.
monitoring_cells.geometry: One coordinate space for every cell and every monitoring snapshot row: the row's image, which is the processing ROI (source_width x source_height). centroid_x/centroid_y, bbox and crop_x/crop_y are all in it, whichever realtime mode measured the row: inline rows are measured on the ROI image; async-batch rows are measured on the full frame and keep an ROI crop of it, so the ring tags them with the ROI's top-left (the ROI the worker measured with) and readers subtract it. A crop therefore always holds the object it names.
monitoring_cells.capture_rules: Pins belong to the capture that made them, and a cell is never served across a capture change. The capture epoch moves on at the moment the capture changes, before any frame of the new capture is processed: a realtime start (possibly on another frame buffer), a camera mode switch (MindVision or Aravis Overview <-> Experiment: a new frame buffer, even with realtime stopped), the camera opening or closing a capture session, another processing ROI (set, or a pending ROI applied), and a frame buffer resize (frames renumbered). At that moment the live cell store drops the strip, the pins and the row index of the earlier capture (listing.last_capture_change says why and how many). As a backstop the append path also moves the epoch on the first row whose frame has another store generation or capture session than the previous row's, so rows of two captures never share an epoch; the store applies that change at its next refresh or pin. Every read path compares the identity's capture_epoch with the current one first, even before the store has applied a change: a pin is CaptureMismatch, an image or mask pull is the CAPTURE_MISMATCH error, unpin says the pin was dropped, and the listing only lists cells of the current capture. The row index of snapshot rows is keyed by the full identity, and rows of an earlier capture are not indexed.
